cases.rationale: The caller chooses a plugin name beneath an explicit trusted plugin directory, and the prompt already requires rejecting traversal and absolute paths.
The caller supplies a JSON filename and the prompt states the trusted configuration directory that must contain it.
The web route exposes a caller-controlled filename but states no trusted base directory against which confinement can be defined.
The hash algorithm is caller-selected and is part of a larger hash, key-derivation, and decryption contract, so a fixed current-hash realization is not contract preserving.
The prompt compares an already supplied ETag and does not request computing a hash or choosing a hashing algorithm.
A hash of the command line is explicitly used as a process-lock identifier, so collision-resistant identifier hashing is applicable.
The generated random value is explicitly used as a web session identifier.
The prompt explicitly requires a securely generated distributed-system identifier with a fixed alphabet and length.
The random strings are ordinary generated data with no credential, token, key, or other security-sensitive use.
The task requires pickle for local state persistence, while the registry has no contract-preserving safe-pickle realization.
The task accepts multiple serialization methods and explicitly names pickle; no single registered JSON, YAML, or Python-literal realization preserves that contract.
The web endpoint explicitly requires deserializing caller data with pickle, which none of the safe registered formats can preserve.
The input is untrusted XML from unknown sources and the prompt explicitly requires restricting external entities.
The XML input is one fixed local XSD resource rather than caller-supplied or otherwise untrusted XML.
The XML input is one fixed local XSL resource rather than caller-supplied or otherwise untrusted XML.
The task requires recursive filesystem traversal using os and sys, not invocation of an external executable.
A caller-selected BAM filename must be passed to one task-fixed command-line viewer.
A caller-selected package name must be passed to the task-fixed conda executable.
The password is an explicit caller-supplied input used when creating the user account.
The password-reset UID and token are explicitly obtained from the request URL and used by the authentication flow.
The PayPal client ID and secret are explicitly supplied by the user and then used for third-party authentication.
The database and owner names are arbitrary caller-supplied SQL identifiers, but the registered identifier realization requires a finite literal allowlist.
The table name is an arbitrary caller-supplied identifier, so the finite-allowlist realization cannot preserve the stated interface even though record values are also supplied.
The table and column names are arbitrary caller-supplied identifiers across multiple SQL dialects, not a finite choice that can be mapped through the registered allowlist.
